name: Brineworks Ghost-Side Street Operative Set
description: A runner's set designed to pass as Tier 2 dockside labor during the day and disappear into Circuit nightlife after dark — the same clothes doing two completely different jobs. The outer layer is a heavy waxed-canvas work shirt in faded teal, its back reinforced with vertical cargo strips that read as tool loops to civilians but function as a modular attachment system for swappable panel inserts: swap in scanner-dampening inserts for a job, swap back to plain canvas for the walk home. The shirt's left interior seam hides a full-length holster channel that accommodates a sidearm or collapsed baton; the right sleeve has a comm-wire conduit running from wrist to collar. Beneath is a dark amber long-sleeve compression base layer with embedded thermal regulation and a port-access panel at the upper back for BCI hardware maintenance. Trousers are a faded indigo heavy denim with reinforced inner thighs, two flat concealed pockets behind the front panels, and a gusset-cut seat that allows full leg extension without pulling. Footwear is a steel-reinforced dock boot in weathered brown with a hidden ankle holster channel in the right boot shaft. The look is completed with a beaten leather-analog work belt with a false-bottom center pouch and a brimmed work cap in matching teal that houses a signal-dampening liner.
functionality: Modular back-panel insert system for swappable scanner-dampening or plain inserts, interior holster channel in shirt seam, comm-wire conduit in right sleeve, BCI port-access panel at upper back, concealed flat trouser pockets, ankle holster channel in right boot shaft, false-bottom belt pouch, signal-dampening cap liner
what_it_says: At first glance, this is a dockworker or freight handler — the teal, the beat-up boots, the work cap. Look closer and the fabric sits too precisely, the belt is too deliberately plain, the cap brim is too stiff. This is someone who studied what labor looks like and built a costume out of function. The runner wearing this respects the work it's imitating — and uses that respect as armor.
worn_by: runners operating in harbor and freight districts
operatives running long-term cover identities as dock or warehouse workers
fixers who broker jobs through Tier 2 labor contacts
runners with BCI implants requiring field maintenance access
manufacturer: Brineworks Fabrication — street label affiliated with Meridian Harbor independent labor networks
story_hooks: A runner has been running a dock-worker cover for six weeks when a real dockworker notices the teal shirt's fabric doesn't absorb sweat the way canvas should — it beads and runs. The worker doesn't say anything, but starts watching.

The modular panel inserts are stored in a locker at a Circuit-district gym. Someone has been in the locker — the inserts are still there, but they've been scanned and logged. The runner now has to decide whether the job is blown or whether whoever scanned them wants something.

The BCI port-access panel has been used recently by someone other than the runner. The connection logs show an unauthorized sync — brief, surgical, and three days ago. Something was read. Possibly something was written.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively functional street operative's ensemble that reads as blue-collar dockside labor at first glance but conceals modular weaponry and augmentation access points throughout. The silhouette is deliberately unremarkable—neither tailored nor overtly baggy—designed to blend into Meridian Harbor's working populations while maintaining tactical mobility. Layered and utilitarian, it projects competence and wear without calling attention.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed but purposeful. The work shirt hangs loose enough for movement and concealment, the compression base layer beneath is snug for BCI interface integrity and thermal regulation, and the trousers are cut with a high gusset to allow full leg extension without strain. Everything moves with the wearer, nothing restricts.
physical_description.primary_material: Outer: heavy waxed canvas (faded teal). Inner: technical compression weave with embedded thermal regulation fibers (dark amber). Trousers: reinforced indigo heavy denim. Footwear: weathered brown leather-analog composite with steel toe and heel. Belt: beaten leather-analog with synthetic core.
physical_description.texture: Waxed canvas is rough and slightly tacky to the touch, with visible wear patterns and creasing from actual use. The compression layer beneath is smooth, almost hydrophobic, with subtle ribbing visible where thermal threads run. Denim is soft from age and repeated washing, with slight fading at stress points. Leather is deliberately distressed—scuffed, creased, broken-in.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded teal work shirt (primary), dark amber compression base layer (visible at collar and cuffs), faded indigo denim (trousers), weathered brown boots, matching teal work cap. Palette reads as sun-bleached harbor labor—blues, ambers, and browns dulled by salt air and industrial exposure.
physical_description.closures: Work shirt: heavy-duty friction-fit button placket with reinforced anchor points. Base layer: friction-fit crew neck, port-access panel secured with magnetic micro-locks. Trousers: traditional button fly with reinforced anchor and flat-seam construction. Boots: speed-lace system with friction-lock aglets. Belt: magnetic clasp with false-bottom release mechanism. Cap: elastic sweatband with internal signal-dampening liner (no visible closure).
distinctive_features: Modular attachment system on shirt back—vertical cargo strips with quick-release panel inserts (scanner-dampening swappable with plain canvas)
Left interior seam: full-length holster channel for sidearm or collapsed baton
Right sleeve: embedded comm-wire conduit running wrist to collar
Base layer upper back port-access panel for BCI hardware maintenance (magnetic micro-locks)
Trousers: two flat concealed pockets behind front panels (blend seamlessly with denim topography)
Reinforced inner thighs (durable for ladder climbing, concealment)
High gusset-cut seat for unrestricted leg extension
Right boot shaft: hidden ankle holster channel
Belt: false-bottom center pouch for small valuables or restricted items
Cap: internal signal-dampening liner (invisible from exterior)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional with deliberate Tier 2 aesthetic—street-level professional tier manufactured by independent labor networks. Signals skilled operative, not corpo or sub-grade.
physical_description.cultural_context: A runner's uniform. Worn by independent fixers, dockside security contractors, augmentation technicians, and unauthorized courier networks operating in Meridian Harbor. The two-job design speaks to someone living between daylight legitimacy and nighttime circuit work—someone who needs to pass as working class by day and disappear into shadows by night. Brineworks affiliation indicates labor-network loyalty, not corpo employment.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately broken-in and worn but not damaged. Canvas shows salt-spray staining and UV fading. Denim has work creases and minor fraying at cuffs. Leather is scuffed and creased from actual use. Nothing is pristine, but nothing is failing—this is a tool that's been used properly and maintained for reliability, not appearance.
